summary: There are no call windows. The DFG Walter Benjamin Programme takes proposals at any time through the elan portal, and a decision takes about 6 months on average. It funds early-career postdocs to carry out their own project, usually for up to two years. In Germany you hold a postdoc position at the host, normally paid at 100%, plus €250 a month for project, travel and publication costs. Abroad you get a fellowship instead (basic amount plus allowances). Carlos appears eligible for the German position, for example with Brouwer or von Oppen at FU Berlin or Hassler at RWTH Aachen: that track has no nationality or prior-Germany-work rules, and he would be changing institution from ICMM-CSIC. He can submit once his dissertation has been handed in (expected around early 2027, with proof of submission and a supervisor statement), but funding only starts after the doctorate is completed. That makes a start around late 2027 realistic. He is not eligible for the abroad fellowship (for example a stay in Copenhagen), because he has not been integrated into the German research system.
eligibility: For postdocs in the early phase after the doctorate (EU 'recognised researcher', R2). DFG sets no fixed number of years since the PhD, and parental leave is taken into account. You can submit once the dissertation has been handed in, but funding starts only after the doctorate is completed. You must generally change institution (not the PhD institution or current one, except with special justification). You must not have worked more than one year at the chosen host when you submit. German position: no nationality or prior-Germany restrictions. Abroad fellowship: you need to have worked at least 3 continuous years in Germany just before the proposal, or have done most of your schooling and higher education in Germany with no more than 3 years abroad for research since the PhD. Carlos does not meet these. The host cannot be for-profit and must allow open publication.
duration: As a rule up to 24 months. The German position and the abroad fellowship modules can be combined. In France, fellowships are limited to 12 months unless you move to a second French institution.
salary: German position: a postdoc post ('postdoctoral researcher and comparable'), usually at 100%, plus €250 a month for direct project, travel and publication costs. The exact pay scale is not stated. Non-university institutes (Max Planck, Helmholtz, Fraunhofer) must guarantee 45% of the position's funding. Abroad fellowship: a monthly basic amount plus foreign, cost-of-living and travel allowances and benefits for children, paid directly to the fellow.

summary: No call is open today (2026-11-04). The 2026 call (HORIZON-MSCA-2026-PF-01) ran from 9 April to 9 September 2026, with results due around February 2027. The next call, HORIZON-MSCA-2027-PF-01-01, is listed as forthcoming on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal and the MSCA site: planned opening 7 April 2027, deadline 8 September 2027 at 17:00 Brussels time. Some sources still mark these dates as provisional, so check the portal before relying on them. European Fellowships last 12–24 months at a host in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country. They pay the researcher living, mobility and, where applicable, family allowances, and pay the host research, training, networking, management and indirect costs. The host PI/organisation writes the proposal with the fellow, submits it, and if funded employs and supervises the fellow. Carlos appears eligible for the 2027 call. His PhD (expected March 2027) would be awarded before the September 2027 deadline, he is well within the 8-year limit, and he has lived only in Spain. That means any host outside Spain (for example Denmark, Germany, the Netherlands, Italy, Sweden or Switzerland) meets the mobility rule. A Spanish host would not. Because his 2025 Copenhagen visit was short, Denmark should still be fine as a host. As an EU national he could also apply for a Global Fellowship to the US or Canada, which adds a mandatory 12-month return phase in Europe. Host institutions often set internal deadlines between April and July, so he should contact host PIs early in 2027.
eligibility: Any nationality (European Fellowships). You need a PhD by the call deadline; a defended thesis counts even before the degree is formally awarded. You can have at most 8 years of research experience after the PhD; career breaks, work outside research, parental leave and long sick leave are not counted. Mobility rule: in the 36 months before the deadline, you must not have lived or had your main activity (work, studies) in the host country for more than 12 months. From 2026, a proposal that scored below 80% the year before cannot be resubmitted with the same host and researcher. Global Fellowships are open only to EU nationals or long-term residents.
duration: 12–24 months (European Fellowships). Global Fellowships are 24–36 months: 12–24 months outside Europe plus a mandatory 12-month return phase. An optional non-academic placement of up to 6 months is possible at the end.
salary: Unit-cost funding. The researcher receives a living allowance (adjusted by the host country's correction coefficient), a mobility allowance, and, where applicable, family, long-term leave and special needs allowances; employer social security costs are included. The host receives research, training and networking costs plus management and indirect costs. The 2027 indicative budget is about €330M for European Fellowships and €58M for Global Fellowships. I couldn't confirm the exact monthly rates from official pages in this search; they are in the MSCA Work Programme 2026–2027.
